newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire envoy whose car killed two still in France.
newsitem.headline: Zaire envoy whose car killed two still in France.

text.p: Zaire's ambassador to France, who was driving a car involved in an accident in which two French schoolboys died, remained in France on Tuesday though he has been recalled by his country, an embassy aide said.
"At the moment, he is still in France, but he is not going to remain here because he has been recalled by his country," the aide said of ambassador Ramazani Baya.
The aide could not say when Baya would leave. He said the envoy had first to carry out unspecified formalities at the embassy and at the French Foreign Ministry.
After that, "we shall see," the aide said.

The Foreign Ministry, which on Monday asked Zaire to allow Baya to stand trial for the deaths, said it expected the envoy to return to Zaire for consultations but also had no timetable for his departure.

"He has stated that he will return to France to be judged if his immunity is lifted," ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told reporters, adding that Baya's diplomatic immunity could not be lifted until he left France.

Zaire has announced it was recalling Baya at Paris's request following the accident in the Riviera resort of Menton on November 23. Police say the ambassador was driving at 100 km an hour (62 mph) in a 45 kph (30 mph) zone.
One of the boys, Raphael Lenoir, 13, died instantly. The other, 12-year-old Ronald Lehartel, died on Saturday. He had been in a coma in hospital since the accident.
Baya has written to the boys' families expressing remorse.
After initially playing down the accident as something that could happen to anyone, the ministry has since hardened its tone and is now demanding that Baya be brought to justice.

"It's shocking that diplomatic immunity might mean that the person who caused this accident...might escape responsibility," Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Monday though he cautioned that he was not making a judgment about the crash.

At the time of the accident, Baya was driving through Menton on his way to visit Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, who has been convalescing at his luxury villa in nearby Roquebrune Cap Martin following cancer surgery in Switzerland in August.
The mayor of Menton was scheduled to meet Mobutu later on Tuesday to urge him to let the diplomat stand trial.

The accident has embarrassed France by putting the focus on the presence of Mobutu, a pariah banned from much of Europe and the United States, in his palatial Riviera mansion during a crisis over hundreds of thousands of refugees in eastern Zaire.
